analysis.title: Rocket Cos. (RKT): Key takeaways from RKT earnings
key_insights: RKT reported 3Q26 adjusted revenue of $2.57bn vs consensus $2.61bn, a modest miss. Rate lock volume was $40.4bn vs consensus $43.5bn, partly offset by a gain-on-sale margin of 2.54% vs consensus 2.45%.
3Q26 expenses were $2.33bn vs consensus $2.36bn and below the company's $2.35bn guide. Lower salary and market expenses were partly offset by higher G&A.

4Q26 adjusted revenue guide is $2.1bn-$2.3bn, about 14.3% below consensus of $2.568bn. The guide assumes continued share gains offset by a smaller mortgage market. RKT expects 4Q refi volumes to fall 50% from 3Q, while industry forecasts are down about 18% QoQ.

4Q26 expense guide is about $2.05bn, roughly 10.5% below the Street, or $1.85bn excluding purchase price amortization ($110mn), SBC ($80mn) and acquisition costs ($10mn). Adjusted expenses are down $165mn QoQ.

The remaining $100mn of annualized COOP cost synergies is expected to come through in 4Q, with a further $100mn planned for 1H27. RKT is targeting vendor, third-party and marketing costs, and may announce a further expense reduction plan at 4Q earnings given excess origination capacity of over $300bn.

Shares were down about 13% since the last earnings report and rose about 4% after hours on the more upbeat cost message. GS says the market had already priced in softer revenue given the move in mortgage rates.

Share gains continued despite the weaker market: purchase share rose 30bps QoQ to 6.5% and refi share rose 120bps to 15.5%. Drivers are closed-end second mortgage volume, Rocket Local and RKT Pro promotions.

Channel margins are tracking near 3Q levels. Gain-on-sale margins have typically compressed when rates rise, but RKT is not seeing that yet. GS suggests this may reflect less balance sheet flexibility across the industry.

RKT thinks the mortgage market forecast for next year is too high (FNMA forecasts $1.87tr). Long-term targets remain 8% purchase share and 20% refi share, with Cooper recapture at 60% and a target of 65% by YE27.
GS keeps a Neutral rating and a $13.00 12-month price target (25x 2027E P/E). Core EPS estimates are cut to $0.53/$0.50/$0.60 for 2026E/2027E/2028E from $0.60/$0.75/$0.85.

market_movers.rationale: GS views 3Q results and the outlook as solid. Lower costs and continued share gains support a baseline level of profitability if rates stay elevated, and the stock keeps option value if mortgage rates fall. Core EPS estimates were cut on weaker revenue.

sector_views.rationale: 4Q market is expected near multi-decade lows, with refi down almost 50% QoQ at RKT. RKT expects the 2027 market to be below the $1.87tr FNMA forecast.

earnings_insights: RKT 3Q26 adjusted revenue reported $2.57bn vs consensus est $2.61bn (reported 10/29/26).
RKT 3Q26 gain-on-sale margin reported 2.54% vs consensus est 2.45%. Rate lock volume reported $40.4bn vs consensus est $43.5bn.
RKT 3Q26 expenses reported $2.33bn vs consensus est $2.36bn and company guide of $2.35bn.
RKT 4Q26 adjusted revenue guide of $2.1bn-$2.3bn vs consensus est $2.568bn (about -14.3%).
RKT 4Q26 total expense guide of about $2.05bn (about 10.5% below the Street), or $1.85bn excluding purchase price amortization ($110mn), SBC ($80mn) and acquisition costs ($10mn).
GS core EPS estimates (new vs old): 2026E $0.53 vs $0.60, 2027E $0.50 vs $0.75, 2028E $0.60 vs $0.85. GS quarterly EPS estimates: 4Q26E $0.10, 1Q27E $0.06, 2Q27E $0.15, with 3Q26 at $0.15.
GS revenue estimates (new vs old): 2026E $11,230.7mn vs $11,048.9mn, 2027E $9,440.7mn vs $11,493.8mn, 2028E $9,999.5mn vs $12,011.8mn.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The rise in long-term rates weakened mortgage origination volumes and pressured RKT's revenue versus the Street.
RKT thinks this forecast is too high, so the 2027 market could be smaller than industry estimates, which are already below $2tn.
RKT's own refi volume is expected to fall about 50% QoQ, a steeper decline than the industry forecast.

risk_factors: Upside risks: recovery in refi volumes, better than expected margins, and stronger expense leverage.
Downside risks: sustained pressure on gain-on-sale spreads, further elevated competition, and an inflated cost base during periods of decreased market demand.
Gain-on-sale margins have typically compressed when rates rise, and that has not yet shown up at RKT.

tension_points.bull_case: Cost cuts (a further $100mn of synergies in 1H27, plus vendor, third-party and marketing savings and possible fixed-cost reductions) and continued share gains support baseline profitability, with option value if mortgage rates decline.
tension_points.bear_case: The 4Q revenue guide of $2.1bn-$2.3bn is about 14.3% below consensus. The refi market is down about 50% QoQ and rates are elevated. GS cut 2027E core EPS to $0.50 from $0.75.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Sustained pressure on gain-on-sale spreads, which GS lists as a downside risk and which has not shown up yet.
